purpose: Compare many-objective selection schemes (LHFiD, NSGA-III, NSGA-II, random) at realistic evaluation budgets on surrogates of the real v3 SD1.5 NAS problem. Fixed before any benchmark run.
training_data: artifacts/nas/seed{1,2,3}/{random,nsga2}/search_results.json (900 real calibration evaluations); latency normalized by each job's reference
scaling: minimization form (CLIP and fidelity negated); fixed affine map with 0 = best value of each objective among the 900 training candidates and 1 = reference point; applied identically for every algorithm before selection

reference_vectors.M6: two-layer Das-Dennis boundary p=2 + inner p=2 shrunk halfway to centroid (42)

variation: identical for all: crossover rate 0.9 (nas_space.crossover), mutation rate 1.0 (nas_space.mutate), no re-evaluation of an execution signature
lhfid_settings: preferences p_m = 1/w_m with zero components floored at the smallest positive component (lhfid) or p_m = 1/M (lhfid_equal); stabilization psi_N = (2 decimals, 10 generations); nadir re-estimated at each detection; self-termination disabled
indicators: exact hypervolume (moocore) in scaled space with reference 1: archive HV (all evaluated) for every algorithm and final-population HV for population-based ones
statistics: per algorithm pair: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 35 (surrogate, seed) cells, Holm-corrected over pairs; a ranking is claimed only if the median difference has the same sign under every one of the 5 surrogates
sanity_check: at 150 evaluations NSGA-II vs random should roughly reproduce the real searches (no consistent difference)
confirmation: for M6 and each algorithm, the run on surrogate 0 with the median final archive HV; from its archive points inside the reference box take the 4-objective-style rule of lock_nas_finalists (best on each objective, then farthest-point) up to 5 points; evaluate them for real on the calibration split in one allocation with a reference run; report surrogate error on these points
